adjudication.attestation_confidence: high for published shorter/longer readings; not fresh image confidence
adjudication.strongest_longer_case: Expected speech content plus Samaritan Hebrew/Greek agreement may preserve an invitation lost before 4Q2 and MT; younger surviving objects can preserve an older ancestral reading.
adjudication.strongest_shorter_case: The abrupt speech formula and immediately following field offer an obvious motive and material for early completion; 4Q2 gives direct ancient Hebrew support for the short junction.
adjudication.mechanism_limit: Repeated Cain/Abel/brother sequence makes loss conceivable, but a simple jump between full repetitions loses more than the two invitation words; exact copying mechanism unproved.
adjudication.dependency_limit: No vote counting: translations may share ancestry, influence or completion; digital aliases and parallel editions are not additional physical witnesses.
adjudication.policy_application: Original-language evidence first; modest age preference for a direct old Hebrew object, never automatic priority. Smooth English and shortest reading are not source-selection rules.

reader_proposal.anchor: And Cain said to Abel his brother[a]
reader_proposal.exact_note_text: The Masoretic Text does not record Cain's words. The surviving wording in 4QGenb (4Q2), as published, supports this shorter transition. The Samaritan Pentateuch and Greek Septuagint include, “Let us go to the field.” The Latin Vulgate has, “Let us go outside”; the Syriac Peshitta similarly includes an invitation to the plain. Whether the invitation was lost from the shorter form or added to complete it is disputed.
